note: Angola's largest banks are BAI, BFA and Banco BIC; BAI's price list for private customers (in force from 24 October 2025, still the one on its site) was read in full for its credit cards, and BFA's and BIC's weren't reached. BAI's Visa Classic, Visa Gold and MULTICAIXA credit cards: yearly fees of 32,600, 42,700 and 7,000 kwanzas (the same in the first and later years), issue fees of 5,175, 18,000 and 5,000, late payment charges of 19,500, 19,500 and 10,000, an over-limit charge of 16,000 on the Visa cards (none on the MULTICAIXA card), and fixed interest of 3.00% a month (2.5% on the MULTICAIXA card). 14% VAT is added to every fee and 0.2% stamp duty on interest, written as tax (this file wrote the Visa Classic's fee with its VAT, 37,164, before the form had a tax term; it is now the fee before VAT, with the VAT as tax). The list's worked examples of the cost of credit assume yearly fees (17,500 and 32,750) that differ from its fee table; the table is written. The Visa Platinum card (100,000 a year) gives no interest rate (N/A), so it isn't written. The renewal, replacement, cancellation and blocking charges, met only when a card is renewed or replaced on request, aren't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a second and third bank: Banco de Fomento Angola (BFA), named above among the three largest, was reached: its price list for private customers (version 74, in force from 1 October 2026), read in full for its credit cards: the BFA Mwangolé Gold and Classic VISA cost 80,000 and 40,000 kwanzas a year and the same to issue, 20,000 for a late payment and 20,000 for going over the limit, and bear 32.00% a year (TAN; the list says the rate's period is yearly); the Lombongo Platinum, Gold and Classic cards cost 25,000, 15,000 and 10,000 a year and the same to issue, 15,000 late and 15,000 over the limit, and bear 29.00% a year. 14% VAT is added to each fee and 0.2% stamp duty to interest, written as tax, as BAI's are; the further 0.1% a month stamp duty on the average balance financed has no form in the game and isn't written; the urgent issue, replacement, cancellation and blocking charges are met only on request and aren't written. Banco BIC's site answered 520 (a server error) and Banco Económico's and Banco Sol's a Cloudflare check. Standard Bank de Angola was added as the third: its price list for private customers (SBAO187, 6 October 2026, the one its site links) draws its text as outlines, so its credit card page (page 20) was read by eye: the Cartão VISA PRESTIGE and Cartão VISA PRIVATE cost 40,000 and 90,000 kwanzas a year, 4,000 and 4,500 to issue, 10,000 for a late payment and 5,000 for going over the limit, and bear 35% and 33% a year (TAN, which its legend calls the annual nominal rate); 14% VAT on each fee and 0.2% stamp duty on interest are written as tax. Its replacement, cancellation, blocking, European delivery and PIN reissue charges are met only on request and aren't written. So Angola has three banks' cards. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: BAI's technical sheet for the Visa BAI Classic lets the holder pay 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% each month, and its pages for the BAI Gold and the MULTICAIXA credit card say the payment is at least 10% of the month's use; written as 10% on all three. BFA's Lombongo leaflet (Classic, Gold and Platinum) and its technical sheet for the Mwangolé Classic give payment of 10%, 25%, 50% or 100% of the monthly balance owed, written as 10%. Standard Bank de Angola's technical sheets for the Visa Private and Visa Prestige set the instalment at a minimum of 10% of the principal owed, written as 10% of the balance (the principal not held apart). No minimum payment is published for BFA's Mwangolé Gold; tried: its adhesion contract (it names a 'minimum to pay' on the statement, with no figure), BFA's technical sheets found (the Mwangolé Classic's and the Lombongo Gold's), the Banco Nacional de Angola (a search in Portuguese found its rules on limits, none on a minimum payment), and BFA's price list (none).
